trigger: an rpm database (sqlite, ndb or bdb) whose headers each carry one large NUL-terminated string region (up to the 32 MiB header cap) that NAME, VERSION, RELEASE, ARCH, VENDOR and PACKAGER all point at; needs a crafted or tampered database or a crafted package installed by root
summary: RpmHeader::string() copies each string tag independently with no per-field cap, while the byte budget charges the header once; probe: 8,388,713-byte blob -> 50,331,648 retained bytes (x6.0), so up to ~6 GiB at the 1 GiB total budget inside the 20 s wall, ~12 GiB with the AppInfo/InvRecord copies; no MemoryMax on the packaged unit. Derived HIGH via the I5(a) raise (reproducible agent-process unavailability on the daily-sync path); the security reviewer's native MEDIUM and the unhappy-path reviewer's HIGH disagreed, the derived band governs the gate. Fix: cap each string tag (oversized) or charge retained string bytes to the budget.
classification_rationale: no bound on retained string bytes; pkgdb_budget.hpp header contract says no allocation from a length not first checked against the byte budget

severity_native: HIGH on the table, MEDIUM in practice
trigger: (a) an rpm database file left on a pacman/apk host with no rpm binary (found with zero rows ends detection, pacman/apk never run); (b) a dpkg status holding only non-installed stanzas on an rpm host (parser keeps them, packages not empty, rpm never read)
summary: read_host_packages treats a found rpm database (L615) and a non-empty parsed dpkg set (L600) as final even when they yield zero emitted rows; the old binary-order cascade needed the tool binary, so a database without its binary is newly reachable. list/query then print an empty result as complete (list_inventory is protected by the no_rows guard). Also reported by happy-path (HP-2) and docs-writer (D2) as the docs saying 'falls through' while the code does not. Borderline on likelihood; derived HIGH by I3 base with E5 no change. Fix: fall through to the next leg when rpm is found with zero rows and when dpkg yields zero installed rows; align banner/README/ADR wording.
classification_rationale: banner, README caveat 3 and ADR say an empty/no-installed-package status falls through; code falls through only on an empty parsed vector

trigger: a failing REQUIRE between sqlite3_open and sqlite3_close in blobs_of_sqlite
policy_floor: manual resource cleanup in NEW C++ not RAII-wrapped (literal reading of the floor; applies to test code; Architect may rule)
summary: raw sqlite3*/sqlite3_stmt* with manual finalize/close; test_installed_apps_pkgdb.cpp:130 already has a unique_ptr<sqlite3, SqliteCloser>. Three-line fix.
classification_rationale: manual cleanup in new test code; the floor text does not exempt tests

trigger: daily sync lands during an rpm transaction on a BDB (RHEL 8) or ndb (SUSE) database: the reader takes no rpm lock (.rpm.lock) and its before/after stamp has coarse (jiffy) ctime granularity on kernels before 6.13, so a write in the same tick as the last pre-stamp write leaves the stamp equal
summary: MANDATORY INVESTIGATION (derived HIGH, speculative so a deferral of the decision, not a dismissal): resolve to verified, likely or refuted before the gate passes. Evidence needed: can the BDB/ndb data file be read mid-transaction and parse as a consistent-looking roster; does the old rpm -qa path take a shared lock that this reader skips. Candidate fix if confirmed: F_GETLK probe on .rpm.lock mapped to the existing locked cause, and a racy-stamp re-check; lane run on alma8 (reinstall loop diffed against rpm -qa). Merges unhappy-path UP-3 and UP-4; sqlite is unaffected (snapshot isolation).
classification_rationale: no lock or racy-stamp handling for in-place-written rpm formats

trigger: dpkg interrupted mid-unpack leaves /var/lib/dpkg/updates/*; this reader does not read it
summary: MANDATORY INVESTIGATION (derived HIGH, speculative): does dpkg-query -W merge the updates journal into what it prints; if it does, the reader lags the old path on an interrupted host. Resolve by dpkg source or one lane check (kill -9 dpkg mid-unpack, diff). If dpkg-query does not merge it, record refuted with the evidence.
classification_rationale: journal not read

trigger: agent stop or reconnect while a package-database read is slow or wedged; the old subprocess leg polled subprocess_cancel_requested (set at stop), the in-process read polls only g_pkgdb_stop, raised in shutdown() after the sync thread joined
summary: stop lambda should also test yuzu::agent::subprocess_cancel_requested() (already available via the included subprocess_runner.hpp) so a slow-but-progressing read ends promptly; a wedged pread stays bounded by the 20 s wall. Folds: no new surface.
classification_rationale: comment claims the stop flag ends the worker; the flag is raised too late to cover agent stop

trigger: operator reads the changelog fragment and inventory.md differences list before upgrade

Also reported independently by docs-writer (D6, D7), happy-path (HP-1, CR-1), quality-engineer (QE-8). README caveats are generated from content JSON: regenerate with plugin_doc_gen, never hand-edit.

trigger: an rpm database that is EMPTY in usr/lib/sysimage/rpm and var/lib/rpm a symlink to a DIFFERENT directory that holds the populated database (a layout the reader never follows); the plugin then runs its pacman leg, finds nothing, and `list`/`query` print an empty, non-degraded result
summary: The up-10 fix suppresses rpmdb:symlink_refused whenever ANY database was read (`if (symlinked_db && !db_read)`), but its stated reason (code comment :788-790, banner) is only the Fedora/RHEL/SUSE layout where var/lib/rpm links to the directory just read. For a link to some other directory the refusal is suppressed too, so a populated database behind a never-followed link reads as "ecosystem none, no failure". Probe on braga (scratch root, real fedora41 fixture, Apple clang): empty sysimage db + var/lib/rpm -> populated dir elsewhere gives eco=none rpm=0 failure=''; the same link with nothing else read gives rpmdb:symlink_refused; the Fedora layout (link to the same dir) reads 4 rows. Derived HIGH (I3, E5, verified) with the trigger a doubly unusual admin layout; which directory is authoritative depends on the host's rpm dbpath, so the wrong outcome is established only where the link target is the dbpath. Borderline, as up-10 was: the Architect may adjudicate the band with an independent adjudicated_by. Fix: suppress the refusal only when the skipped link resolves to a directory already read (compare st_dev/st_ino of the link target with the opened directory descriptor), else keep symlink_refused; add the layout to the tests (empty db + link elsewhere => symlink_refused; empty db + link to itself => none).
classification_rationale: the code comment says the suppression is for a link to the directory just read; the code suppresses for every link once a database was read

trigger: a dpkg status file hand-edited to mixed-case or repeated-blank Status words, which dpkg-query read, is now refused as dpkg_status:corrupt (degraded, rows kept) until dpkg rewrites it
summary: The Status vocabulary check (kWants/kFlags/kStates, 9 bad words tested) is a deliberate difference from the old path, stated only in the ADR-0016 bullet and the dpkg_status_parsers.hpp banner. README caveat 5, docs/user-manual/inventory.md "What else is different" and the changelog fragment do not say it. Vocabulary itself verified against dpkg main (pkg-namevalue.c wantinfos, eflaginfos, statusinfos; fields.c f_status). Fold: one sentence in each of the three, README fences and plugin-docs JSON regenerated with the repo generator, never hand-edited.
classification_rationale: required doc items 2 (user-manual section) and 3 (changelog fragment) of the shared preamble list

severity_native: NICE (derived MEDIUM; native and derived disagree)
trigger: an ndb or Berkeley DB host where an administrator made .rpm.lock unreadable to the agent account (mode 0600 or 0640 root-only); the open gives EACCES, mapped to rpm_ndb:unreadable / rpm_bdb:unreadable on every read; the old rpm -qa never opened that file
summary: rpm_transaction_refusal maps any open error other than ENOENT to its own cause, so an unreadable lock file refuses the read (fail closed, named token, stored rows kept). Mapping verified by probe (mode 000, non-root). Reachability unresolved: rpm is believed to create the file 0644, not verified, and the lane step already owes a check that the unprivileged account can open it. Not a code change (failing closed is right); document the token and the mode assumption. Fold with the docs batch and prove on the lane.
classification_rationale: README caveat for the lock-file read is missing the unreadable-lock-file case (shared preamble required doc item 2)

trigger: operator reads the manual text about the dpkg journal and the apk leg
summary: Wording and scope precision, folded together: (a) manual/README/ADR say a pending dpkg journal makes "a dpkg host" locked, but dpkg_updates_failure runs whether or not a dpkg database exists, so an rpm host with a stale dpkg tree and a digits-named journal file answers dpkg_updates:locked with no fall-through (code :426, pinned by a test); (b) inventory.md:373 says an empty rpm database falls through to "pacman and apk", but list/query have no apk leg (installed_apps_plugin.cpp:429-468), only list_inventory does; (c) README caveat 3 says a stanza "dpkg itself would reject" while the reader now also refuses forms dpkg accepts (see r2-d1).
classification_rationale: prose precision only; the domain agent for (a) is architect, who confirmed the behaviour is the ruled one

trigger: no test for an empty first rpm candidate followed by a failing second one, or for an empty first candidate with a link elsewhere
summary: The code is correct for the first (a later-candidate failure is returned with no rows) but unpinned. Fold two sections with the r2-up-10b fix, reusing the emptied-sqlite helper plus a corrupt database.
classification_rationale: missing coverage of a fix-delta branch, bounded blast radius (SHOULD at most, not a floor)

trigger: the only held-lock test uses an open-file-description lock in the same process, not the classic POSIX lock another process (rpm) holds
summary: F_GETLK seeing an OFD lock proves the query, not rpm's lock class; a macOS probe showed a child-held classic lock is reported and released correctly, nothing runs it on Linux. Deferred as a task with the lane false-lock check. Not a false-green: the test observes what it asserts.
classification_rationale: test coverage of the real lock class is missing; blast radius bounded

trigger: a digits-only name longer than 10 characters in var/lib/dpkg/updates; the reader answers dpkg_updates:locked
summary: Raised from memory of dpkg's journal-name rule (a maximum length) with no source at hand.
classification_rationale: comment at :338-339 says the digits rule is dpkg's own

summary: Fixed in 085292788c: PkgDbBudget::kept_left and charge_kept (agents/shared/pkgdb_budget.hpp:111), RpmHeader::text returning string_view and rpm_package_from_header(h, budget) charging every kept string before its copy (agents/shared/rpmdb_parsers.hpp:152, 245-253), Limits::rpm_max_kept_bytes = 8 MiB set at read_rpm_dir (installed_apps_pkgdb_read.hpp:120, 697). Re-verified in round 2 by two independent reviewers: six aliased tags pass only if 6L <= 8 MiB; a 32 MiB string fails on the first charge; the aliased-string test goes red if charge_kept is removed.

Fixed in 085292788c: dpkg is the answer only when a stanza is `installed` (installed_apps_pkgdb_read.hpp:760), an empty rpm database continues to the next candidate (:775-786), and symlink_refused needs `symlinked_db && !db_read` (:791); tests cover all five sections of the r1 ruling. A residual of the same fix (a link to a different directory after an empty database) is recorded as r2-up-10b-empty-db-with-link-to-other-dir.

Fixed in 085292788c: tests/unit/test_rpmdb_parsers.cpp blobs_of_sqlite owns the connection (before the REQUIRE on the open result) and the statement (declared after it, finalized first) with std::unique_ptr; no manual cleanup remains in new test code (round 2 grep of the delta).

Fixed in 085292788c, refined in 9ee0a151bd: rpm_transaction_refusal (installed_apps_pkgdb_read.hpp:612-629, called at :690 for ndb and Berkeley DB only, after the first stamp and before the first read) opens .rpm.lock through the database directory descriptor (leaf not followed, O_NONBLOCK) and asks fcntl(F_GETLK) for a whole-file write lock; locked refuses the read; ENOENT is not locked; any other open error or a failed query is its own cause. It never takes a lock. Resolved to likely from the rpm source in the round 1 ruling (every writer holds the transaction lock, no reader does). Closed by construction; the held-lock cases run on Linux only and the lane must show them executed.

Fixed in 085292788c: dpkg_updates_failure (installed_apps_pkgdb_read.hpp:355-388, called from read_dpkg at :426) lists var/lib/dpkg/updates by name through walk_dir_capped, a digits-only name is dpkg_updates:locked with the status packages discarded, an absent directory is no journal, a link, non-directory or failed listing is a named failure. Premise verified in round 2 from dpkg source (lib/dpkg/dbmodify.c: modstatdb_open calls cleanupdates for every mode but lock-only, and cleanupdates parses every digits-named file of the updates directory; write-back and unlink only at write access), so dpkg-query -W printed the merged view.

Fixed in 085292788c: the readers' expired predicate is g_pkgdb_stop || yuzu::agent::subprocess_cancel_requested() (installed_apps_plugin.cpp:419-424); the latch is set only at agent stop and never cleared in production; include and link verified in round 2; lexical gate mutations pin it.

Fixed in 085292788c (changelog fragment, docs/user-manual/inventory.md, README, ADR-0016); round 2 residuals are recorded as r2-d1-status-vocabulary-undocumented, r2-cx1-rpm-lock-file-eacces and r2-docs-wording-batch.
Fixed in 085292788c: tests/test_installed_apps_pkgdb_wiring_lexical.py pins the failure-return shape and the stop predicate (mutations 15-17); the script passes (rc 0, 2 tests).

Fixed in 085292788c and 9ee0a151bd: tests/unit/test_installed_apps_pkgdb.cpp covers the ctime stamp, the ndb/bdb shell row cap, short read and EINTR in fd_source, and the progress handler; new cases cover each r1 blocking fix.
Fixed in 085292788c; round 2 wording residuals are folded into r2-docs-wording-batch.

Refuted in round 2 against dpkg source: lib/dpkg/dbmodify.c update_file_filter selects digits-only names and, when a name is longer than DPKG_DB_IMPORTANT_MAXLEN, calls ohshit ("updates directory contains file ... whose name is too long"), so dpkg and dpkg-query themselves fail on such a name; the old path therefore degraded too, and dpkg_updates:locked (a named degraded answer, rows kept) is the same class of outcome, not a defect.
refuted_by: curl of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guillemj/dpkg/main/lib/dpkg/dbmodify.c, lines 63-85 (update_file_filter: digits-only, ohshit when l > DPKG_DB_IMPORTANT_MAXLEN) and 380 (cleanupdates called for every mode but lock-only)
refuted_by_reporter: governance runner, round 2 (a governance agent; not the change author)

trigger: a populated usr/lib/sysimage/rpm (first candidate, accepted at once) with var/lib/rpm a symlink to a different directory that holds a database file
summary: README caveat 3 (and the generated plugin JSON), changelog.d/8411 line 6 and ADR-0016 ~line 2026 say a populated directory read 'beside' a hiding link is refused and (README) 'never' published; a_link_is_unresolved() runs only when a database is about to be accepted and at loop end, over links recorded EARLIER in the candidate order, so the layout in TRIGGER publishes the sysimage roster with no failure. Derived HIGH by I6 raised under (a): the change advertises a data-integrity control as in force that is not enforced (the Gate 7 'a narrowed change still advertising the original control is I6 false assurance' clause). Fix is docs-only: say 'read after it' (links recorded before the accepted directory) and state that a link on a later candidate is not examined (README caveat 3, regenerate content/plugin-docs/installed_apps.json with plugin_doc_gen, changelog bullet, ADR sentence at ~2026, and the read_host_packages comment). The code gap itself is fix8411-2.
classification_rationale: prose asserts a refusal the code does not perform in one candidate order; the code follows spec R1-2 ('already-recorded' links)

trigger: populated real usr/lib/sysimage/rpm plus var/lib/rpm a symlink to a different directory holding a database (for example a relocated live database beside a stale sysimage copy)
summary: read_host_packages returns at the first populated directory, so a link on a LATER candidate is never examined (no symlink_refused) and a roster that rpm -qa may not read is published as complete. R1-2 asked only for already-recorded links and that is implemented correctly; 3a3f82b1f9 accepted the same layout. Fix options: probe every candidate with symlink_hides_database before accepting (the Fedora, RHEL 9, older and SUSE layouts still pass by DirId), or accept the residual and document it (fix8411-1).
classification_rationale: the ADR principle 'a database behind a link this reader never follows is a refusal' is enforced in one candidate order only
waiver_rationale: Pre-existing relative to the fix range: the same layout or state is accepted identically at 3a3f82b1f9, and the fix did not widen it. Deferred under the run's scope rule set by the requesting session (a finding that is not a defect in the fix's own change is a deferred item, not a blocker for the fix). The derived band is recorded unweakened and no independent adjudication was obtained: the gating rule would otherwise hold this row, so the requester or a non-author owner confirms the deferral when the issue is filed.

trigger: an operator whose host shows dpkg_status_d:corrupt for a zero-byte, comment-only, two-stanza or lone not-installed status.d file, or rpmdb:symlink_refused for a populated directory read after a hiding link, or rpmdb:not_regular
summary: docs/user-manual/inventory.md was accurate at 3a3f82b1f9 and the fix widened the rules without touching it: the status.d bullet still says only 'one unparseable regular file in status.d' degrades; the Symlinks bullet limits symlink_refused to a directory this reader did not read; the not_regular line (~424) omits a regular file where an rpm database directory belongs. README, ADR and changelog were updated. Rests on required-doc items 2 and 6 (the ADR-0016 row names this page and it accrues one entry per change; the earlier round of this PR added the Symlinks clause here). Stays MEDIUM: the remedy still works and the stored rows are kept. Fold: update both bullets and the not_regular line to match README caveats 3 and 5.
classification_rationale: required doc (user-manual section for a changed operator-visible failure and remedy) is now incomplete; I7 absence, not wording

trigger: a host degraded by a zero-byte or two-stanza status.d file, a regular file at an rpm candidate directory, a populated directory beside a hiding link, or rpm_bdb:corrupt; the token and log name no file or directory
summary: Only status.d has a stated remedy (remove the file or add a leading dot) and it gives no way to find the file; no remedy sentence exists in the manual, README, ADR or changelog for rpmdb:not_regular, rpmdb:symlink_refused (populated-beside-link case) or rpm_bdb:corrupt, and the rpmdb tokens do not say which of the three candidate directories. Suggested text: a find command for non-hidden, non-.md5sums files in /var/lib/dpkg/status.d (each must hold exactly one stanza); remove the file at the candidate path for not_regular; retarget or remove the link or stale directory for symlink_refused; restore or rebuild the database for rpm_bdb:corrupt. Fix at the same sites as fix8411-3.
classification_rationale: required doc item 2 (operator remedy for a failure token the change introduces or widens)

trigger: BDB damage that reads as a free or overflow page (a zeroed page, a flip to type 0 or 7) or a same-tick in-place rewrite
summary: README caveat 3 says a damaged record makes the read corrupt 'so a partial roster is never published' and caveat 5 says any other page type is 'never skipped'; the residuals (a hash page zeroed or flipped to type 0 or 7 is skipped, narrowing but not closing the class, stated only in a code comment at rpmdb_parsers.hpp:507; the stamp-granularity residual is stated in caveat 5) are absent from the README, ADR and changelog for the BDB case. HIGH rejected: nothing is destroyed and the next read re-converges. Fix: name the zeroed/flipped-page residual beside 'never skipped' in README caveat 5 and the ADR (the code gap is fix8411-15).
classification_rationale: a residual of a data-integrity control is documented in code only

trigger: a maintainer reads the contract block above read_rpm_bdb and re-adds the skip
summary: The block still says 'only hash pages are read' (line 429) and 'Every other non-hash page type holds no package record and is skipped' (line 434); the code now skips only types 0 and 7, answers unsupported_format for 2 and corrupt for every other type. The fix made a pre-existing sentence false, next to the completeness branch. Replace with: a free page (0) and an overflow page (7) are skipped, type 2 is unsupported_format, any other non-hash type is corrupt.
classification_rationale: comment contradicts the adjacent control-flow branch; derived INFO (no operational impact)

trigger: the list action and a daily-sync tick overlap, or an abandoned bounded worker is still reading, while rpm writes a rollback-journal database
summary: The new comment says 'nothing else in this process opens rpmdb.sqlite'; Linux has no single-flight (only the macOS profiler cache is), so two overlapping runs of this same reader hold two connections on one inode and one run's ScopedFile close drops the other's main-file fcntl locks. The conclusion (exposure near nil: WAL isolation lives in -shm, the immutable open takes no locks, the change stamp backstops a torn read) still holds. Proposed: 'list /var/lib/dpkg/status.d and check each file (not *.md5sums, not dot-named) holds exactly one stanza: look for a zero-byte or comment-only file, two Package lines, a not-installed Status, or a hand edit. classification_rationale: a remedy is present; it is thin for the cases and silent on the cost of removal

trigger: a WAL-mode rpmdb.sqlite with a non-empty -wal, read by two overlapping reads of this reader (an abandoned bounded worker outliving its call)
summary: The comment rewritten in a3dee735cf says 'rpm's own sqlite backend runs in WAL mode ... so no main-file lock is held across reads'. A WAL connection holds a SHARED lock on the main file while open (the immutable open, used when -wal is absent or empty, takes none). Verified read-only by the governance runner on one host, macOS with Python's bundled sqlite 3.53.4: an exclusive lockf on the SHARED range was refused while a read-only WAL reader was open and granted before it opened and after it closed; the vcpkg sqlite and Linux were not tested. The near-nil exposure conclusion still holds (an abandoned worker's result is discarded and the change stamp backstops a torn read). Truth owner: cpp-safety. Fix: 'a WAL connection holds a main-file SHARED lock while open (an immutable open takes none), which the early close would drop, but an overlapping read is an abandoned worker whose result is discarded, and the change stamp backstops a torn read.'
classification_rationale: a lock claim in a comment contradicts sqlite WAL behaviour; harmless to the conclusion, so I9
